roster.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
roster.outlook: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on a record-setting pace heading into Seattle's Week 9 game against the Cardinals. Though the Seahawks were crushed by Chicago in Week 8, Smith-Njigba put up another big game with six catches for 118 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets. The star wideout is up to a league-leading 985 receiving yards through eight weeks, putting him on pace to break the NFL's all-time record for receiving yards in a season. He'll have a prime opportunity to add onto his impressive stat line in Week 9, as the Cardinals are tied for 25th in the league with 23.7 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts on the campaign.

roster.name: Saquon Barkley
roster.outlook: Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, Saquon was otherwise held in check with 54 scrimmage yards in a dismal 27-10 loss to Washington. Philadelphia does not appear likely to trade Barkley to a contender, leaving him primed for a revenge game against his former squad, the New York Giants, in Week 9. New York is allowing 128.1 rushing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.

roster.name: Rashee Rice
roster.outlook: Rashee Rice returned in Week 8 from a two-game absence due to a hamstring issue and caught his second touchdown of the season in Kansas City's loss to the Broncos. In four full games this season, Rice has managed a 20-243-2 line on 25 targets as Patrick Mahomes' top downfield option, but he has yet to receive double-digit targets in any game. That's a volume he reached four times in eight contests in 2025. Rice will look to put the injury further behind him in Week 9 against a Jets secondary that ranks 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Colston Loveland
roster.outlook: Colston Loveland will look to remain a high-volume option as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Loveland was solid again in a Week 8 win over the Bears, bringing in seven of nine targets for 65 yards but losing a fumble. The second-year tight end has now brought in six or more receptions in four of his last five games, and he's found the end zone in two of his last three. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 22nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Jadarian Price
roster.outlook: Jadarian Price is coming off an inefficient return from IR heading into Seattle's Week 9 clash against the Cardinals. Price moved past a chest injury to lead Seattle's backfield in carries against Chicago on Monday Night Football, but he garnered just 29 yards on 10 totes and eight yards on two catches. He shared RB snaps fairly equally with Zach Charbonnet, and if the duo continues in a timeshare, both players may have a limited week-to-week fantasy ceiling. The Cardinals do present a relatively favorable matchup, as they're middling or worse in most statistical categories versus running backs.

roster.name: Jameson Williams
roster.outlook: Jameson Williams will look to keep it rolling as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Williams kept his touchdown streak and recent dominance alive in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, reeling in four of six targets for 70 yards and a touchdown. The speedy wideout has now logged 11 catches for 208 yards and a whopping five touchdowns in his last three outings. He'll face a Dolphins defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs on the year.

roster.name: Parker Washington
roster.outlook: Parker Washington has been held to a single catch twice in Jacksonville's last four games but is averaging a team-high 61.7 receiving yards per game and has four TDs through seven games. His occasional down games keep Washington out of the set-and-forget WR1 range, but he's a high-end fantasy WR2 for a Week 9 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 177.6 yards per game to WRs. Baltimore has given up plenty of yards to the position but has held wideouts to just five TDs. There are numerous mouths to feed in Jacksonville's high-octane passing game, but Washington continues to have the most upside among the team's pass catchers.

roster.name: J.K. Dobbins
roster.outlook: J.K. Dobbins may have lost his hold on the top job in the Broncos' backfield. In a Week 8 comeback win over Kansas City, it was rookie Jonah Coleman who got the biggest workload and who scored the winning touchdown on a five-yard run. Dobbins recorded just seven carries, his second straight game getting single-digit touches, and his woeful 3.3 yards per carry doesn't make a strong case for a bigger role. With RJ Harvey on injured reserve, Dobbins should retain the No. 2 job for the next few weeks. The veteran might be able to make a splash on limited carries in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and which ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Zach Charbonnet
roster.outlook: Zach Charbonnet will look to build upon an uneventful season debut when the Seahawks host the Cardinals in Week 9. Charbonnet logged his first game action since January this past Monday against Chicago and finished with 23 yards on six carries along with six yards on three catches. He shared the backfield primarily with Jadarian Price (12 touches), and that arrangement may cap both players' weekly production moving forward. Arizona does present a decent matchup, as the Cardinals are tied for 20th in the NFL with 18.2 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs this season.

roster.name: Chase McLaughlin
roster.outlook: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He made all three of his field goal attempts despite the heavy rain in the Week 8 win over the Falcons. On the season, he's converted all 19 of his field goal tries and all 17 of his point-after attempts. Despite his incredible season, McLaughlin is in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Bears defense that's allowed just 5.0 kicking points per game through seven weeks this year.

roster.name: Bryce Young
roster.outlook: Bryce Young will look to bounce back from a tough Week 8 performance in the Panthers' Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Young has really struggled over Carolina's last two contests, completing just 37 of 68 pass attempts for 372 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. Young has been playing through a knee injury since the Week 3 loss to the Browns, which could be hindering his performance. However, he could bounce back in Week 9, as Denver's defense has given up 20.7 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.outlook: James Cook brings a six-game scoring streak into the Bills' Week 9 matchup against a stingy Vikings defense. He topped 20 carries in three straight contests and five of seven overall. Cook added five catches for 79 yards in his last two games after just 31 yards in his first five. Minnesota has allowed only four rushing scores through seven games, but a healthy 4.6 yards per carry in a blitz-heavy scheme. With Cook assured of heavy usage, he appears poised for solid production.

roster.name: Nico Collins
roster.outlook: Nico Collins is coming off a rare dud, as the Giants held Houston's star WR to six yards in Week 7, which is 50 yards fewer than Collins' previous season low. After a Week 8 bye to stew over his down game, Collins should come out motivated to bounce back in a Week 9 road game against the winless Chargers. The Chargers rank in the middle of the pack against WRs, allowing 132.7 yards per game to the position. Collins remains a low-end fantasy WR1 until further notice.

roster.name: DeVonta Smith
roster.outlook: DeVonta Smith missed yet another game for the Eagles due to a balky hamstring. Smith has played in just four contests in 2026 in what has been a lost season overall for 2-6 Philadelphia. If he is somehow able to suit up in Week 9, he would be facing a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 184.9 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.outlook: D'Andre Swift will look to build on a high-volume performance as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Swift was, for the most part, stymied by a tough Seattle front in Week 8, averaging just 2.6 yards per carry, but he still put together a monster game with three touchdowns and 69 yards off a season-high 27 rushes. The veteran has directly benefited from the absence of position mate Kyle Monangai in the last four weeks, which can especially be seen through his seven touchdowns in that stretch. With or without Monangai active, Swift should have a tough time, especially if he can't find the end zone, against a Tampa Bay front that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Rome Odunze
roster.outlook: Rome Odunze figures to be a top option in Chicago's passing game again as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Odunze finished Week 8 with his second-highest yardage of the season, bringing in four of six targets for 87 yards. The third-year wide receiver has eight catches for 156 yards in the last two weeks, which is his most productive two-game stretch so far this campaign. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Christian Watson
roster.outlook: Christian Watson will look to heal from a broken rib ahead of Green Bay's Week 9 matchup at New England. Watson injured himself in the second quarter of Week 8 against the Panthers, but he returned to the game in the third quarter after a brief trip to the hospital. Even with these setbacks, the starting wideout finished the game with an impressive stat line, hauling in eight of 10 targets for 113 yards. He's now sitting at a receiving line of 42-708-6, which is career-high in both receptions and yards. He'll face a Patriots defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to WRs in the last three weeks.

roster.name: Justin Herbert
roster.outlook: Justin Herbert is coming off another shaky performance, as he failed to throw a touchdown and got picked off twice in the Chargers' Week 8 loss to the Rams. The 28-year-old quarterback has a miserable 5:10 TD:INT through seven games this season, and the offense under Mike McDaniel appears to be broken beyond repair, as the winless team has scored more than 17 points only once all year. Herbert remains a very risky play heading into a Week 9 meeting with a Texans defense that has also underperformed, sitting 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Travis Kelce
roster.outlook: Travis Kelce caught five of seven targets for 67 yards in Kansas City's Week 8 loss to the Broncos, his best performance since delivering a 9-101-1 line in Week 2. The veteran tight end remains one of Patrick Mahomes' most trusted options, and Kelce has a shot at his first 1,000-yard effort since 2022 if he can maintain his current pace. He could be poised for solid numbers again in Week 9 against a Jets defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Matthew Golden
roster.outlook: Matthew Golden remains a high-volume option ahead of Green Bay's Week 9 matchup at New England. Golden surpassed 10 targets for the fifth time this season in a Week 8 win over Carolina, and he finished the night with seven catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher has now posted a 43-619-4 receiving line on 82 targets this season. He should have plenty of opportunities to stay hot against a Patriots defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers in the last three weeks.

roster.name: Eddy Pineiro
roster.outlook: Eddy Pineiro will hope the 49ers' Week 8 bye has helped him get back on track against the Raiders in Week 9. Piniero missed an extra-point attempt in each of his previous two contests before the bye, and he's made just six of nine field goal tries this season. All three of his misses have come from 50-plus yards, but it's still a notable downturn after the veteran kicker went 6-for-7 on attempts from that distance last season. He could be mostly busy with PATs against a Las Vegas defense that has had 27 PAT tries versus only 14 FG attempts against it so far this season.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.outlook: T.J. Hockenson will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Hockenson was a key piece in Minnesota's passing game once again in a Week 8 loss to Detroit, reeling in four of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown. The veteran has now registered five targets in back-to-back games, and he's found the end zone in each as well. He'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this season.

roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.outlook: Jonathan Taylor set season lows with 12 touches for 47 yards in the Colts' 42-7 Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. Indianapolis got down big early and had to abandon the run. The Cowboys have enough talent on offense to repeat the scenario, but it's more likely that the Colts keep things close enough for Taylor to capitalize on facing a Dallas defense that has been among the most generous in the league to RBs, allowing 11 total TDs to the position through eight games. Taylor has eight rushing TDs in eight games, accounting for more than half of the Colts' offensive touchdowns this season. He'll be a fantasy RB1 if he's in his usual role, though it's possible Indianapolis limits Taylor's usage as trade rumors swirl around the star RB.

roster.name: Malik Nabers
roster.outlook: Malik Nabers has crossed the 100-yard receiving mark in four-straight contests for the Giants. Nabers has racked up a staggering 36 catches for 509 yards and two touchdowns over that span. He has drawn an insane 51 targets during that time period, an average of nearly 13 opportunities per clash. In Week 9, the G-Men will face a scuffling Eagles squad. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.

roster.name: Cam Skattebo
roster.outlook: Cam Skattebo retained his starring role for the Giants last game, gaining 121 scrimmage yards and scoring a touchdown in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. Tyrone Tracy went on Injured Reserve following the victory, leaving Devin Singletary as the only other legitimate option at running back behind Skattebo. Though talks of a trade for Jonathan Taylor have intensified, nothing appears imminent heading into a tasty Week 9 clash with Philadelphia. The Eagles have been torched on the ground in 2026, allowing 131.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. Likewise, the Eagles have given up 10 rushing scores, which is tied for 24th in the NFL.

roster.name: Bucky Irving
roster.outlook: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of the Buccaneers' offense in the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has rushed for over 100 yards in three of his last four games, averaging a whopping 121.8 rushing yards per game during that span. He now ranks fifth in the NFL in rushing yards per game (91.0) while scoring six total touchdowns in eight appearances this season. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is expected to continue leaning on the run game, which has led the Buccaneers to a 3-1 record over the last four weeks-a positive sign for Irving's outlook. However, he is in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Chicago defense that has given up just 18.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs through seven contests this year

roster.name: Tucker Kraft
roster.outlook: Tucker Kraft will look to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Kraft found the end zone once again in Week 8 against the Panthers, finishing the game with six catches for 53 yards and his score. The tight end has now posted a 35-350-3 receiving line on 49 targets this season, and he's found the end zone in back-to-back games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack in fantasy points allowed to TEs this season.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.outlook: Trevor Lawrence has thrown seven touchdown passes across Jacksonville's last two games, so he remains a top-10 fantasy QB option ahead of a Week 9 road game against the Ravens. He has just one touchdown pass across two road games this season, but Jacksonville's offense should get plenty of opportunities with the Ravens unlikely to sustain drives in the expected absence of Baltimore's top two QBs, Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe). Baltimore's defense has allowed an 11:4 TD:INT ratio while ranking in the middle of the pack against the pass. Despite his lackluster road production, Lawrence has thrown touchdown passes on a league-high 8.6% of his passes this season en route to a 17:4 TD:INT overall.

roster.name: Jordan Mason
roster.outlook: Jordan Mason should remain a part of a two-punch backfield in Week 9 as the Vikings play the Bills. Mason led Minnesota's backfield with eight carries in a Week 8 loss to the Lions, but he finished with just 20 yards compared to Aaron Jones' five carries for 22 yards. The current timeshare between the two could continue to keep both in check, but Buffalo ranking 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs is favorable.

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.outlook: Braelon Allen's successful five-week run as the Jets' lead back appears set to end in Week 9 against the Chiefs with the pending return of Breece Hall (quad). Allen had at least 16 touches in every outing with Hall sidelined, capping it off with a career-high 147 yards in Week 8. While he's earned a role in the team's backfield, his workload share is unclear. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.3 yards per carry further limits Allen's potential production.

roster.name: Ollie Gordon II
roster.outlook: Ollie Gordon will bring consistent volume into the Dolphins' Week 9 matchup with the Lions. Since taking over as the team's lead back, Gordon has at least 17 carries in four of his last five games, though he's seen a minimal amount of work in the passing game, snagging just six passes. Detroit has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs, mainly due to opponents passing on them at will, which Miami isn't equipped to do. With volume paramount for the position, Gordon is a safe bet to pile up carries, creating a nice floor that can be elevated if he finds the end zone.

roster.name: Juwan Johnson
roster.outlook: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Johnson has really underperformed in the Saints' last two games, catching just one of five targets for seven yards during that span. Despite this recent lack of production, Johnson ranks third on the team in receiving yards (255), targets (38) and receptions (26) while catching three touchdowns across seven contests. Johnson could bounce back against a Cleveland defense that's given up 15.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

roster.name: Chuba Hubbard
roster.outlook: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain a vital piece of the Panthers' offense in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Hubbard was one of the few bright spots in Carolina's Week 8 loss to the Packers, totaling 119 yards and a touchdown on 29 touches. He ranks 10th in the NFL in touches per game (20.0) and 11th in total yards per game (98.6), which bodes well for his outlook going forward. Hubbard could thrive against a Broncos defense that's allowed 25.3 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.outlook: Zay Flowers and the Ravens host the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. He was held without a catch on five targets during Baltimore's 36-10 Week 8 loss. With Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both leaving the game with injuries, Flowers struggled mightily to get anything going. The Ravens could be forced to start Joe Fagnano (knee) against the Jaguars' 29th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs, but the uncertainty at the QB position greatly lowers Flowers' fantasy appeal.

roster.name: Spencer Shrader
roster.outlook: Spencer Shrader is quickly losing his luster as the reeling Colts continue to struggle on offense. He still leads the league with 19 made field goals, but Shrader has slowed down significantly after an 18-for-18 start through Week 6. Shrader has gone just 1-for-3 on field goal attempts over the past two games while the Colts have been outscored 58-17 in that span. It's tempting to cut bait given his recent downturn, but fantasy managers should give Shrader one more chance to get back on track in Week 9 against the Cowboys, who are giving up 26.6 points per game, which is the sixth-most in the NFL.

roster.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
roster.outlook: Omar Cooper will look for consistent chances when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. After consecutive 100-yard outings, Cooper failed to collect a target despite a 79% snap share in Week 8, with Adonai Mitchell and Garrett Wilson dominating opportunities. Despite a banged-up secondary in Week 8, Kansas City is allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wideouts, which includes just two touchdown catches. The Jets' offense could be forced to throw more frequently from behind, but the passing game isn't strong enough to support multiple receivers on a regular basis.

roster.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
roster.outlook: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to stay hot as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Gibbs recorded another monster performance on the ground in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, rushing the ball 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown, with two catches for 15 yards as well. The superstar has now surpassed 100 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's found the end zone in all but one outing this season. He'll take on a Dolphins defense that's ranked a favorable 27th in fantasy points allowed to running backs so far this campaign.

roster.name: A.J. Brown
roster.outlook: A.J. Brown's availability for the Patriots' Week 9 game against the Packers is uncertain due to lingering knee and ankle injuries. Brown was a late-week addition to the injury report with a knee issue that has seemingly persisted since last season, in addition to an ankle problem that previously cost him four games. When healthy, Brown has been targeted regularly but has struggled with drops, posting a season-high 48 yards in Week 7. Should he play, he'll face a Packers defense that has allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers but has been vulnerable to their opposition's top option, allowing 70 or more yards six times.

roster.name: Ladd McConkey
roster.outlook: Ladd McConkey came out of the Chargers' bye looking healthy, and he was one of the few bright spots on offense for the team in a Week 8 loss to the Rams. The third-year wideout caught four of six targets for 86 yards, and over six games this season -- only two of which he saw a full snap share in -- he's produced a 17-286-1 line on 24 targets. If McConkey can stay on the field, he figures to continue being Justin Herbert's top downfield option, on a winless team that's been trailing early and often in 2026. McConkey will face an underperforming Texans secondary in Week 9 that ranks a stunning 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Joe Burrow
roster.outlook: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are in Spain for a Week 9 overseas tilt against the Falcons. In Week 8, he completed 38 of 48 pass attempts for 462 yards with five TDs and three INTs, and he had three carries for 10 yards and another score during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win. Burrow recorded season highs in passing yards, completion percentage, TDs, and INTs, and he has posted a 13:3 TD:INT ratio over his last three outings. Burrow faces a Falcons defense allowing 18.7 fantasy points per game (10th) to opposing QBs.

roster.name: Cameron Dicker
roster.outlook: Cameron Dicker hasn't missed a kick in four straight games, converting all three of his field goal attempts in a Week 8 loss to the Rams but failing to even see a PAT for a second straight contest. The Chargers' offensive struggles limit Dicker's opportunities despite his accuracy, and the advantage of playing his home games indoors. Dicker will look for a little more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans team that's giving up 24.3 points per game, 18th in the league.

roster.name: Jalen Coker
roster.outlook: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Carolina's top receivers in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Coker has been relatively quiet since returning from injury in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, catching just nine of 22 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown over his last three contests. Despite this, Coker ranks second on the Panthers in targets (7.3), receptions (4.5) and receiving yards per game (60.7) this season, suggesting more production could be in the near future. Coker could struggle in Week 9, however, as Denver's secondary has allowed just 6.8 yards per target to opposing wideouts this year.

roster.name: Brock Purdy
roster.outlook: Brock Purdy should be well-rested off the 49ers' bye week for a Week 9 clash against Las Vegas. Purdy will be looking to bounce back from his first multi-turnover game of the campaign, as he threw two interceptions in a Week 7 loss to the Falcons. Despite that performance, Purdy still ranks in the top five leaguewide with a 110.1 QB rating in 2026. He could also be getting a big boost Week 9, as injured wideouts Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) all have a chance to return from absences. Purdy should be able to find success against the Raiders, who have allowed a 103.2 QB rating this season, third-worst in the NFL.

roster.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
roster.outlook: Deebo Samuel has a chance to return from a two-game absence for San Francisco's Week 9 tilt against Las Vegas. Samuel hurt his hamstring in Week 5 against Seattle and hasn't played since, but the 49ers' Week 8 bye allowed him time for extra rest. Mike Evans (Achilles) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) also have a chance to return to San Francisco's wideout corps following absences of their own, so the team's passing game could be getting a big boost. The outlook is positive for all of the 49ers' wide receivers given that the Raiders have allowed 10 receiving touchdowns to the position this year, tied for third-most in the NFL.

roster.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
roster.outlook: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to make a return to the end zone as the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9. St. Brown logged seven receptions for 46 yards and recorded one rush for 10 yards in a Week 8 win over Minnesota. The featured pass catcher has remained a dominant option week in and out, but he hasn't posted a touchdown since Week 3. He'll face a Miami defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs this season but 18th in the last three weeks.

roster.name: Dallas Goedert
roster.outlook: Dallas Goedert has caught at least four passes in four-straight games for the Eagles. He has amassed 28 targets over that span. Unfortunately, Goedert is averaging less than 45 yards receiving per contest during that time period. He has also been held out of the end zone. With backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center, Goedert's prospects may not be getting any better. In Week 9, the Eagles will face a Giants defense allowing just 184.9 passing yards per tilt, which us third in the NFL.

roster.name: Blake Corum
roster.outlook: Blake Corum should continue to have a big role in the Rams' backfield in Week 9 against the Commanders. Corum logged five fewer carries than backfield make Kyren Williams this past Sunday versus the Chargers, but Corum led the team with 73 rushing yards and also scored a touchdown for the fourth straight contest. After taking fewer than 10 totes four straight weeks, Corum has averaged 14 carries across his past two contests and seems to have regained his role as Los Angeles' 1B option next to Williams' 1A role. Washington has been pretty tough on running backs so far this season, tying for 10th in the league with 15.5 fantasy points allowed per game to the position.

roster.name: Will Reichard
roster.outlook: Will Reichard will aim to get back on track as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Reichard didn't get much usage in a Week 8 loss to the Lions, missing a field goal attempt from 57 yards and converting his sole extra-point try. Even with a field goal miss in each of the last two weeks, the third-year kicker still sits at 18 of 20 on the year, and he's gone a perfect 10-for-10 on XPAs. Buffalo has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to kickers.

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense in the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Bijan struggled along with the rest of the Falcons' offense in a Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, rushing 19 times for 76 yards while failing to haul in his lone target. Despite this poor performance, Robinson ranks third in the NFL in touches per game (21.9) and fifth in total yards per game (122.9), so the production will likely follow. He's could thrive against a Bengals defense that just allowed Tony Pollard to account for 137 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 8 win over the Titans.

roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.outlook: Josh Allen has his work cut out for him when the Bills face the Vikings in Week 9. He ran for his ninth touchdown in seven games during Week 8 and tossed two touchdown passes for the fourth time this season. He's matchup-proof, but Allen will face constant pressure from Minnesota's heavy blitzing scheme that's allowed only four touchdown passes and 81 rushing yards to opposing quarterbacks through seven games.

roster.name: Kenneth Walker III
roster.outlook: Kenneth Walker has been held out of the end zone and below 100 scrimmage yards in back-to-back games, both Kansas City losses. The star running back still sits third in the race for the NFL rushing crown with 770 yards, just behind Bijan Robinson's 780 yards and Jahmyr Gibbs' 773 yards, but he might need more help from Patrick Mahomes and the passing game to get defenses to stop loading up against him. Walker will look to bounce back in Week 9 against a Jets defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.outlook: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' top wideout if active for the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has been sidelined for two consecutive games due to a concussion and a foot injury. During that span, the Buccaneers completed just seven of 14 pass attempts for 64 yards and one touchdown, proving Egbuka's importance to the passing game. He's expected to lead the team's WR room against a tough Bears secondary that's allowed just 29.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through seven games this season.

roster.name: DJ Moore
roster.outlook: DJ Moore will look to overcome a knee injury and help the Bills in Week 9 against the Vikings. It's been simple: when Moore plays, he's heavily involved, amassing 25 targets in three games. Minnesota is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, surrendering just four touchdown catches and 7.4 yards per target, but if he's on the field, Moore will have the volume necessary to be a viable lineup consideration.

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.outlook: Luther Burden will look to stay busy as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Burden stayed hot in a Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, bringing in seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets across the last three games, and he's surpassed 50 receiving yards in all but two games this season. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
roster.outlook: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top pass catchers in the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Despite catching just two of five targets for six yards in the Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, Pitts finished tied for the most receptions in the game. Prior to last week's loss, Pitts appeared to be finding his groove, averaging 5.0 receptions, 41.3 yards and 1.3 touchdowns per game from Weeks 5 through 7. He's expected to bounce back against a Bengals defense that's given up 15.9 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this year.

roster.name: Courtland Sutton
roster.outlook: Courtland Sutton set new season highs in catches and receiving yards during the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, but he still came away with just a 4-53-0 line on four targets. The struggles of quarterback Bo Nix, as well as the offseason addition of Jaylen Waddle, have reduced Sutton's target volume considerably from 2025, and he's on pace for only 79 targets this season after topping 120 in each of the prior two years. He'll try to make do with new role in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator, and which is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Kyle Monangai
roster.outlook: Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Monangai has sat out the last four weeks with thumb and toe issues. The second-year ball carrier recording a 30-146-2 rushing line before his inactive streak makes it even more frustrating, so he'll hopefully get back to practice sooner rather than later. If he is healthy against Tampa Bay, he'll face a defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

roster.name: Tyler Shough
roster.outlook: Tyler Shough is expected to leads the Saints' offense into the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Through seven contests this season, Shough has thrown for 1,721 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions while averaging the most pass attempts per game (39.0) in the NFL. With this high passing volume, Shough should continue to find fantasy success going forward. However, he could really struggle against a tough Browns defense in Week 9 that's given up just 17.1 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: Alvin Kamara
roster.outlook: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain the Saints' top pass-catching running back in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Kamara has received seven targets in two of New Orleans' last four games, proving his value to the team's passing attack. While not the most effective rusher at this stage in his career, Kamara has averaged 43 total yards on 10.5 touches per game through six contests this season. He could struggle against a tough Browns defense that's allowed just 28 total receptions to running backs through eight games this season.

roster.name: Malik Washington
roster.outlook: Malik Washington's usage is on a slight decline as the Dolphins prepare to face the Lions in Week 9. Washington has just nine targets over the last two games, and while he scored his first touchdown of the year in Week 8, he's averaged under 10 yards per reception in three straight games. Detroit is allowing the ninth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers, but they have been far more vulnerable to tight ends. Washington will require higher volume if he's to return meaningful fantasy production.

roster.name: Tre Tucker
roster.outlook: Tre Tucker put his boom-bust tendencies on full display in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets, failing to catch his only look from Kirk Cousins one week after producing a 5-103-1 line on 12 targets against the Rams. Tucker is Las Vegas' top option at wide receiver, but Brock Bowers is the focal point of the passing attack, and Michael Mayer and Ashton Jeanty get their share of the target volume as well. Tucker is still on pace for a career-best campaign with a 29-474-4 line on 48 targets through eight games, but his floor will always be risky. He'll look to bounce back in Week 9 against a 49ers secondary that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Ja'Marr Chase
roster.outlook: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to Spain for a Week 9 overseas tilt against the Falcons. He brought in 11 of 16 targets for 141 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 8 overtime victory. Chase eclipsed 100 receiving yards for the first time all season while pacing the team in receptions and targets, but fellow wideout Tee Higgins (10-155-2) finished slightly ahead in yardage. Chase owns a 43-492-6 line on 61 targets through seven contests and will look to build upon that versus Atlanta's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (30.1) to WRs.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.outlook: Drake London will look to bounce back from a tough Week 8 performance when the Falcons plays the Bengals in Week 9. London struggled along with the rest of Atlanta's offense in a rainy loss to the Buccaneers, catching just one of six targets for eight yards. However, he's still been one of the NFL's most productive receivers with Michael Penix at quarterback this year, averaging 5.5 receptions and 90.7 receiving yards per game. London will have a good opportunity to rebound against a Cincinnati secondary that's allowed 33.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receivers this season.

roster.name: Breece Hall
roster.outlook: Breece Hall is poised to return from a five-game absence due to a quad injury when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. In Hall's absence, Braelon Allen shined and has likely earned at least a portion of the carries, leaving Hall's role uncertain. Pairing that with a matchup against a Kansas City defense that's allowing just 3.3 yards per carry, Hall doesn't offer a solid floor or much upside in Week 9.

roster.name: Quinshon Judkins
roster.outlook: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to face the Saints in Week 9. He rushed 11 times for 25 yards and caught both of his targets for 24 yards during Cleveland's 27-6 Week 8 loss. Judkins handled 11 of 12 carries out of the backfield but took a backseat to Dylan Sampson in the passing game. Judkins will aim to bounce back against a New Orleans defense that ranks last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.8) to opposing RBs.

roster.name: Lamar Jackson
roster.outlook: Lamar Jackson is heading to the IR after taking just one snap for the Ravens in Week 9. He missed the prior three contests with a high-ankle injury, and now thumb surgery could end his season. Tyler Huntley took over, but he had to exit with a toe injury, forcing emergency third-string QB Joe Fagnano into action. More will be known about Jackson's status after he goes under a very small knife.

roster.name: David Montgomery
roster.outlook: David Montgomery (groin) sat out Houston's last two games prior to the Week 8 bye, and it sounds like he may not be ready to suit up in Week 9 against the Chargers. Even if Montgomery is cleared to return, he'll be a risky flex option, as he was averaging a meager 2.7 yards per carry prior to getting injured while splitting carries with Woody Marks. The Chargers rank among the league's 10 most generous run defenses, allowing 124.6 yards per game on the ground. Running backs have scored nine total touchdowns in seven games against the Chargers, with eight of those TDs coming on the ground.

roster.name: Sam LaPorta
roster.outlook: Sam LaPorta will look to get back on track as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. LaPorta had another quiet performance in Detroit's Week 8 win over the Vikings, bringing in three of five targets for 33 yards and logging one rush for two yards. After an impressive stretch heading into a Week 6 bye, the starting tight end has now logged just four catches for 51 yards in the last two weeks. LaPorta will face a Miami defense that's ranked a favorable 30th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Josh Jacobs
roster.outlook: Josh Jacobs will again have an asterisk next to his name as the Packers face the Patriots in Week 9. Jacobs has been active the last two weeks, and while he's averaged an inefficient 2.3 yards per carry on 32 attempts, he's salvaged his performances with three total touchdowns in this stretch. The veteran ball carrier also could be at risk of not playing in the near future, as the NFL continues to investigate his alleged physical incidents. This makes him an uncertain play, especially against a New England defense that's ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

roster.name: Jason Myers
roster.outlook: Jason Myers will look to rebound from a poor performance when Seattle faces off against Arizona in Week 9. Versus the Bears in Week 8, Myers had a field goal attempt blocked and also missed an extra-point try in a Seahawks loss. The PAT miss was just his second of the season, and Myers is a solid 15-for-17 on FG tries, so the rough game shouldn't affect his job security. He could get plenty of opportunities to kick against the Cardinals, who are giving up a league-worst 29.8 points per game.

roster.name: Woody Marks
roster.outlook: Woody Marks looks set to retain the lead role in Houston's backfield for a juicy Week 9 matchup with the Chargers, leaving him firmly in the fantasy RB2 range. David Montgomery hasn't played since getting banged up early in Week 5 against the Titans, and he may not be ready to return after Houston's Week 8 bye. Marks has averaged 18.7 touches over the past three games while recording at least 81 scrimmage yards in each of those three games. He should continue to pile up yardage against a Chargers defense that is allowing 124.6 rushing yards per game, and Marks has a nice opportunity to find the end zone for the first time since Week 4, as RBs have produced nine TDs in seven games against the Chargers.

roster.name: Matthew Stafford
roster.outlook: Matthew Stafford will try to help the Rams move above .500 for the first time this season with a win in Week 9 against Washington. Stafford was pretty quiet against the Chargers this past Sunday, throwing for just 157 yards with one touchdown and one interception, but his performance was good enough to lead his team to a second straight victory. The veteran quarterback continues to rely heavily on star wideout Puka Nacua with Davante Adams (hamstring) expected to remain sidelined for multiple more games. Stafford has a prime matchup against the Commanders, who have given up the third-most fantasy points per game (24.6) to quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: Tyler Allgeier
roster.outlook: Tyler Allgeier may be asked to log a heavy workload for the Cardinals in Week 9 against Seattle. Fellow RBs Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) are both dealing with injuries, leaving Allgeier to potentially carry the run game on his shoulders versus the Seahawks. Allgeier thrived with that responsibility this past Sunday in an overtime win over Dallas, logging 147 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries along with 44 yards and another score on five catches. However, he could find the sledding tougher against a Seattle defense that is allowing just 3.28 yards per carry to running backs, the second-best mark in the league.

roster.name: CeeDee Lamb
roster.outlook: CeeDee Lamb led the Cowboys in receiving last game. Unfortunately, he managed just 58 yards and failed to find the end zone in the 33-30 OT loss to Arizona. Lamb has accumulated a staggering 41 targets over the last three contest, though has failed to cross 75 yards receiving in any of those contests. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.

roster.name: Justin Jefferson
roster.outlook: Justin Jefferson will aim to ramp up his output as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jefferson brought in five of nine targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in Week 8 against the Lions, finding the end zone for the fourth time this season. The superstar wide receiver is on pace to finish the season with the fewest catches and yards of his career, and he's yet to record a 100-yard receiving game. Luckily, he'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.outlook: Garrett Wilson's usage has been inconsistent ahead of the Jets' difficult Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs. After showing frustration following a three-target Week 7, Wilson was peppered with 12 looks in Week 8-the third time he's amassed double-digit targets. However, he's drawn only 27 total looks in the Jets' other five games. Kansas City has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers but was without corners Mansoor Delane and L'Jarius Sneed in Week 8. Week 9 absences would help Wilson's potential.

roster.name: Javonte Williams
roster.outlook: Javonte Williams was largely held in check last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 56 yards rushing on 24 carries. He was also held out of the end zone for just the second time all season. The workload remains stellar, though, as Williams now has a staggering 49 carries in the last two contests alone. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense that has been subpar against the run. Indy is allowing 131.8 rushing yards per tote, which is 27th in the NFL.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren turned 10 targets into just 18 yards in his return from a two-game absence due to a groin injury in the Colts' 42-7 Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. That performance sums up the sorry state of Indianapolis' passing game, but Warren's volume remains elite for a TE. He's back to being a set-and-forget starting option at the position now that he's healthy, especially with a favorable Week 9 home matchup on tap against the Cowboys. Dallas' defense is allowing 51 yards per game to TEs and has given up four TDs to the position, surrendering 26.6 points per game overall.

roster.name: Dak Prescott
roster.outlook: Dak Prescott scored two total touchdowns last game for Dallas. However, Prescott passed for one touchdown or fewer for the fifth time in six contests. Dak was also held under 200 yards passing for just the second time in 2026. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.

roster.name: Mike Evans
roster.outlook: Mike Evans is expected to return from a one-game absence for the 49ers' Week 9 matchup against Las Vegas. Evans was held out of the Week 7 loss to Atlanta due to a lingering Achilles issue, but San Francisco's Week 8 bye enabled him to get some much-needed rest. It still bears monitoring the veteran wideout's practice participation throughout the week, though, as Achilles injuries can be tricky. Should Evans indeed suit up, he'll face a struggling Raiders defense that has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game (23.9) to wideouts this season.

roster.name: Michael Wilson
roster.outlook: Michael Wilson could play in Arizona's Week 9 matchup against Seattle despite dealing with two broken ribs. The wideout suffered the injury this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, but he returned to the game after getting hurt and finished with eight catches for 111 yards and one touchdown on 15 targets. Wilson thrived with both Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew under center, so the switch to Minshew as the Cardinals' starting QB shouldn't impact Wilson's production if he's able to suit up in Week 9. However, the ribs issue plus a stout Seattle pass defense that has given up the fewest fantasy points per game this season (14.3) to wideouts could hurt Wilson's production.

roster.name: Caleb Williams
roster.outlook: Caleb Williams will look to stay solid as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Williams pieced together another solid outing in Chicago's Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown. The starting quarterback has now thrown for 860 yards and four touchdowns in his last three games, and he's passed for 240 or more yards in all but one outing this season. He'll shift focus to a Tampa Bay squad that's ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
roster.outlook: Chris Godwin will look to bounce back from a lackluster Week 8 performance when the Buccaneers face the Bears in Week 9. He struggled along with the rest of Tampa Bay's receiving corps in last week's rainy win over the Falcons, as Baker Mayfield completed no passes. If Emeka Egbuka (foot) misses his third consecutive game in Week 9, Godwin would operate as Tampa Bay's top wideout. Even so, the Buccaneers have attempted just 14 passes over the last two weeks, so Godwin's fantasy production is capped by the team's limited passing volume. Nonetheless, Godwin could find success against a Chicago secondary that's given up 9.5 yards per target to opposing wideouts through seven games this year.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.outlook: Jordan Addison will seek to build off a team-leading performance as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Addison led Minnesota with 66 receiving yards on three catches in a Week 8 loss to the Lions. The speedy pass catcher has posted a modest 16-249-1 receiving line across six games this season. He'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.

roster.name: Mark Andrews
roster.outlook: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Jaguars for an AFC showdown in Week 9. He caught three of four targets for 14 yards during Baltimore's 36-10 Week 8 defeat. Andrews finished second on the team in receptions and third in targets, but the entire Ravens offense struggled with Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both forced out with injuries. Andrews has compiled an underwhelming 29-218-1 receiving line on 41 targets through seven games this season. Fantasy managers should look elsewhere, with the 31-year-old squaring off against Jacksonville's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (11.0) to TEs.

roster.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
roster.outlook: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on multiple field goal attempts in four consecutive games prior to Houston's Week 8 bye. The standout kicker should pick up where he left off in Week 9 against the 0-7 Chargers, who have allowed 14 made field goals in seven games while giving up 25 points per game. Fairbairn has missed just one kick all season and remains a set-and-forget starter at the position. It's worth checking whether Fairbairn was dropped in your league during his Week 8 bye.

roster.name: Puka Nacua
roster.outlook: Puka Nacua continues to take on a monumental target share for the Rams heading into a Week 9 matchup versus the Commanders. With Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined the past two weeks, Nacua has racked up 19 receptions for 148 yards and two touchdowns on 22 targets. Quarterback Matthew Stafford targeted other wideouts just seven times this past Sunday in a win over the Chargers, so Nacua is likely to continue to draw a lot of attention in the passing game, though that should be the case even after Adams returns. The Commanders present a great opportunity for Nacua's continued success, as they rank 20th in the NFL with 21.0 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.outlook: Trey McBride doesn't seem likely to slow down despite a quarterback change in Arizona with a Week 9 tilt in Seattle on tap. McBride logged seven receptions for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in an overtime win over Dallas in Week 8, extending his streak of games with seven-plus catches to eight to begin the season. Five of his receptions (including his TD catch) and 52 of his yards came after Gardner Minshew took over at quarterback in the third quarter, so the Cardinals' switch to Minshew as the starter in Week 9 doesn't figure to slow down McBride's production. However, the Seahawks present a tough challenge, as they've given up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (5.4) to tight ends this season.

roster.name: Tetairoa McMillan
roster.outlook: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Following his huge performance against the Lions in Week 4 (14-192-2), McMillan has cooled off, catching just 16 of 26 targets for 184 yards and no scores over Carolina's last three games. Despite this, McMillan ranks 11th in the NFL in receiving yards per game (81.1) 12th in targets per game (9.3), which suggests more production is coming in the near future. However, he's in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Denver secondary that's allowed just 27.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Tee Higgins
roster.outlook: Tee Higgins and the Bengals battle the Falcons in a Week 9 interconference clash in Spain. He caught 10 of 11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime victory in Week 8. Higgins led the team in yardage and TDs while finishing second in both receptions and targets behind Ja'Marr Chase (11-141-1). Higgins has tallied at least 148 receiving yards in three of his last four outings, and he'll aim to stay hot against an Atlanta defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed per game (30.1) to WRs.

roster.name: Drake Maye
roster.outlook: Drake Maye will look to continue providing elite production when the Patriots face the Packers in Week 9. While his volume was low, Maye completed a season-high 80% of his passes in Week 8, tossing multiple touchdowns for the fifth straight week while running for a score for the third time in four games. The Packers figure to offer fair resistance, allowing multiple touchdown passes just twice all season, snagging as many interceptions as touchdowns (10) while surrendering just 6.2 yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest mark in the league.

roster.name: TreVeyon Henderson
roster.outlook: TreVeyon Henderson will look to return from an illness that cost him Week 8 when the Patriots face the Packers in Week 9. Henderson has just 14 carries over his last three healthy games and has added only five catches all season. Always a big-play threat, Henderson doesn't appear to be in a spot to pop a long run against a Packers defense that's allowed only four runs of 20 or more yards through eight games.

roster.name: Brandon Aubrey
roster.outlook: Brandon Aubrey connected on three field goals and three extra points for Dallas last game. Unfortunately, Aubrey also missed a kick from 50-plus yards out, and the Cowboys ended up losing to Arizona by three points in overtime. Still, Aubrey has now made three field goals and three extra points in each of the last two games for the Cowboys. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 9 versus the folding Colts. Indy is allowing 27.8 points per clash, which is 30th in the NFL.

roster.name: Travis Hunter
roster.outlook: Travis Hunter has touched the ball on offense at least once in each of Jacksonville's last three games. The full-time cornerback is slowly increasing his role on offense heading into a Week 9 game against the Ravens, but he still isn't playing enough to warrant consideration in fantasy formats that don't reward his defensive contributions. Hunter has put forth just one fantasy starter-worthy performance this season on offense, catching all four of his targets for 59 yards and a TD in Week 6 against the Texans.

roster.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
roster.outlook: Aaron Jones will aim to make the most of his opportunities as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jones shook off a knee injury and ended up playing in Week 8 against the Lions, but he logged a season-low five carries and 22 rushing yards, with two catches for 18 yards as well. The veteran's output moving forward is likely to remain capped with Jordan Mason sharing the backfield, but the pair could carve out some success versus a Buffalo defense that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Khalil Shakir
roster.outlook: Khalil Shakir continues to provide stability in Buffalo's passing game ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. Shakir has recorded at least six targets in five of seven outings, going for 50 or more yards four times. It's a modest floor with only one touchdown catch, and it's even lower facing a Minnesota defense that's allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers, including just four touchdowns in seven games.

roster.name: Isaiah Likely
roster.outlook: Isaiah Likely had a surprisingly poor game for the Giants his last time on the field. Likely managed just two catches for 12 yards in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. Likely had managed double-digit targets in each of the previous three games for the G-Men, so the lack of looks was eye-opening. Still, new quarterback J.J. McCarthy was working under center and targeted star wideout Malik Nabers with reckless abandon. Likely should see more work in Week 9 versus the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 235.4 passing yards per contest, which is 24th in the NFL.

roster.name: Xavier Worthy
roster.outlook: Xavier Worthy continues to struggle in his third NFL season. The Kansas City wideout has handled at least six targets in four straight games and six of seven in 2026, but that steady volume has resulted in just a 27-230-1 line on 41 total targets. Worthy is being used on downfield routes less often this year, with his 8.8 aDOT being a career low, but Andy Reid hasn't been able to consistently scheme him into open space where he can use his elite speed. If the front office adds reinforcements at wide receiver by the trade deadline, Worthy's role could be squeezed further. He'll try to put together a breakout performance in Week 9 against a Jets secondary that ranks 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
