roster.name: Derrick Henry
roster.outlook: Derrick Henry and the Ravens hope to snap a three-game losing streak when they host the Jaguars in Week 9. He had 11 carries for 53 yards and Baltimore's lone TD while catching both of his targets for seven yards during Week 8's 36-10 loss. Henry has failed to top 60 rushing yards since Week 5, and things likely won't be any easier for him moving forward with Lamar Jackson (thumb) possibly done for the season. Henry will face a Jaguars defense that ranks second-best in the league at defending opposing RBs, allowing 17.3 fantasy points per game.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.outlook: Brock Bowers produced his first multi-TD game of the season in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets, turning 10 targets into seven catches for 92 yards and two scores. The star tight end remains the top downfield option for Kirk Cousins, and over six games since making his belated 2026 debut, Bowers has amassed a 41-547-5 line on 62 targets. He could be poised to make another big impact in Week 9 against a 49ers defense that's tied for 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Patrick Mahomes
roster.outlook: Patrick Mahomes bounced back from a two-game touchdown drought to throw three TDs in Week 8, but it wasn't enough as Kansas City lost to the Broncos and ceded first place in the AFC West. Despite a lack of consistent help at wide receiver, something that could be addressed at the trade deadline, Mahomes is on pace for his best passing yards total since 2021. With a 12:4 TD:INT ratio through seven games, he could produce 30-plus touchdowns for the first time since 2022. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 9 against a Jets defense that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Harrison Butker
roster.outlook: Harrison Butker's job security continues to shrink. The veteran kicker missed a 54-yard field goal in the fourth quarter of a Week 8 loss to the Broncos, forcing Kansas City to go for a touchdown on its next possession to try and overcome a four-point deficit, rather than give Butker a chance to play hero. He's missed at least one FG in three straight games, and his 66.7% success rate (12-for-18) through seven games is over 20 points lower than his 2025 performance. Head coach Andy Reid hasn't yet made a move to replace Butker, but the team did sign Justin Tucker to its practice squad last week. If Butker gets a chance to turn things around in Week 9, he'll be facing a Jets team allowing 23.5 points per game, 16th in the league.

roster.name: Michael Mayer
roster.outlook: Michael Mayer continues to provide consistency as a secondary option for Kirk Cousins in the Raiders' passing attack. The fourth-year tight end has caught at least three passes in seven of eight games this season, putting together a 36-351-1 line on 43 targets. Brock Bowers is the clear No. 1 option for Cousins, but Las Vegas' lack of depth at wide receiver has allowed Mayer to surge to a career season, and his 36 catches for 351 yards through eight games are already new personal bests. Mayer will take aim at a 49ers defense in Week 9 that's tied for 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen has recorded at least six receptions in four of seven appearances for the Colts this season and is likely to maintain a prominent role in Week 9 against a Dallas defense that's giving up 11.9 catches, as well as 164.1 receiving yards and 1.0 TD per game to WRs. Allen leads the Colts with 34 catches despite missing a game, and his 325 receiving yards are just five shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. However, the 34-year-old Allen has scored just one TD in his last 17 regular-season games, dating back to last season with the Chargers. He remains a rock-solid, high-floor flex play for Week 9.

roster.name: Devaughn Vele
roster.outlook: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Vele has recorded over 50 receiving yards in four of seven appearances this season, ranking second on the team in yards (348), targets (46) and receptions (33). He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's high-volume passing attack, as Tyler Shough currently leads the NFL with 39.0 pass attempts per game. Vele could struggle in Week 9, however, as Cleveland's secondary has allowed just 10.1 yards per completion this season.

roster.name: Chase Brown
roster.outlook: Chase Brown and the Bengals take on the Falcons for a Week 9 showdown in Spain. He rushed 12 times for 55 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 46 yards during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in Week 8. Brown lost a fumble but managed to out-touch Samaje Perine 20-5, a good sign for Brown's fantasy outlook. Next up is a Falcons defense allowing 28.1 fantasy points per game (30th) to opposing RBs after giving up 324 rushing yards in their last outing.

roster.name: George Pickens
roster.outlook: George Pickens was held to just 48 yards receiving last game for Dallas. This was his lowest receiving total since the second week of the season. Pickens has just 10 targets combined over the last two games and was seen leaving the field early following the OT loss to Arizona, meaning there could be trouble in paradise. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.

roster.name: C.J. Stroud
roster.outlook: C.J. Stroud posted an 11:1 TD:INT ratio in seven games prior to Houston's Week 8 bye, but the Texans are just 2-5 heading into a Week 9 road game against the 0-7 Chargers. Pass defense hasn't been the Chargers' problem, as they're allowing the seventh-fewest yards per game through the air and have limited QBs to an 8:6 TD:INT ratio. Stroud has often been asked to carry Houston's offense with the team's two main RBs both averaging no more than 3.5 yards per rushing attempt, but the Texans may rely more on their defense and running game in Week 9 to exploit the Chargers' weaknesses. Stroud is a viable fantasy option in deeper formats, but he has a low Week 9 floor based on the matchup.

roster.name: Stefon Diggs
roster.outlook: Stefon Diggs found the end zone again last game for Washington. Diggs snagged three balls for 38 yards and the score in the 27-10 win over the Commanders. Diggs has scored in back-to-back outings, and five times overall in 2026. However, in Week 9, Diggs will face a stellar Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.

roster.name: Christian McCaffrey
roster.outlook: Christian McCaffrey's hamstring issue will be worth keeping an eye on ahead of San Francisco's Week 9 matchup against the Raiders. McCaffrey suffered a mild hamstring strain Week 7 against Atlanta, but a well-timed Week 8 bye provided an opportunity for him to get abundant rest. Should McCaffrey be unable to suit up in Week 9, however, rookie Kealon Black is likely to take on lead RB duties for the 49ers. Whichever player leads the team's backfield has a juicy matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yielded a league-worst 5.31 yards per carry to running backs this season.

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.outlook: Omarion Hampton remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Keaton Mitchell got seven touches and Kimani Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Hampton hasn't found the end zone since Week 4, and while he's nominally at the top of the depth chart, his current usage holds little appeal. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Chris Olave
roster.outlook: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Olave ranks fifth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (90.9) and sixth in receptions per game (7.0) through seven contests. Additionally, quarterback Tyler Shough is averaging a league-high 39.0 pass attempts per game, which suggests Olave will continue to produce at a high level going forward. He's in for a tough Week 9 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 29.8 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Kyren Williams
roster.outlook: Kyren Williams will likely continue to share the Rams' backfield in Week 9 against Washington. Williams tallied a modest 56 yards on 16 carries against the Chargers in a win this past Sunday, but he managed to get into the end zone for the fifth time over his past five games. He's faced competition for carries of late from Blake Corum, who has tallied 28 totes for 166 yards and two TDs over the past two weeks. Both Williams and Corum could battle for running room against the Commanders, who are yielding just 3.63 yards per carry to running backs, which ranks seventh-best in the NFL.

roster.name: Jaylen Waddle
roster.outlook: Jaylen Waddle caught his second touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, but his overall numbers remain disappointing, The former Dolphin has just a 29-315-2 line on 51 targets through eight games, and the struggles of quarterback Bo Nix have prevented Waddle from finding a rhythm in his new offense. Waddle has been targeted 10 or more times only once in those eight games, while last season's No. 1 wide receiver for Denver, Courtland Sutton, handled double-digit targets six times in 2025. Waddle will look for more volume in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator, and which is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.outlook: Jayden Daniels has thrown for at least 215 yards in each of the last two games for Washington. He also has three touchdown passes over that span. However, in Week 9, Daniels will face a stellar Rams pass defense.  Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.outlook: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 9 matchup versus the Raiders well-rested following his team's Week 8 bye. Kittle had his snaps managed each of the first two weeks following his January surgery to repair a torn Achilles tendon, but amid multiple injuries to the 49ers' WR corps, the star tight end logged at least an 85% offensive snap share (and at least six targets) in each of his past five games. San Francisco could get multiple of the injured wideouts back for Week 9, but Kittle should still be a big part of the passing game, as he ranks fifth among NFL tight ends with a 22.4% target share this season. He'll face a Las Vegas defense that has given up eight touchdowns to tight ends, tied for second-most in the league.

roster.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
roster.outlook: Rhamondre Stevenson will look to lead the Patriots backfield again in Week 9 against a stingy Packers defense. Stevenson earned double-digit touches in seven of New England's first eight games and has at least 13 carries in four of his last five contests, despite sharing backfield touches with TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner. Green Bay has allowed 10 rushing touchdowns through eight games, which Stevenson may need for solid Week 9 production, as the Packers are allowing just 3.96 yards per carry.

roster.name: Josh Downs
roster.outlook: Josh Downs scored his first TD of the season, accounting for the Colts' lone score in their 42-7 Week 8 loss to Jacksonville, but he fell short of 50 receiving yards for the fifth consecutive game. Downs continues to start in Indianapolis' low-octane passing game and has drawn at least four targets in every game. Ahead of a Week 9 home game against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 164.1 receiving yards and one TD per game to wide receivers, Downs' consistent involvement, coupled with Dallas' defensive struggles, makes him a viable fantasy WR3 or flex option for Week 9.

roster.name: Jake Bates
roster.outlook: Jake Bates will look to stay solid as the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9. Bates missed his first kick of the season in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, but he still converted two of three field goals and nailed his sole XPA. The second-year kicker has now gone 12-for-13 on field goal attempts and made all 23 of his extra-point tries across seven outings. The Dolphins have ranked in the middle against fantasy kickers this campaign.

roster.name: Tanner McKee
roster.outlook: Tanner McKee continues to struggle under center for the Eagles, though admittedly he is working with limited help. Though running back Saquon Barkley returned from injury in the loss to Washington, staring wideouts Devonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks remained sidelined, and the right side of the offensive line is still a work in progress. McKee had two turnovers while failing to throw a touchdown against the Commanders. In Week 9, McKee will face a much-improved Giants pass defense. The G-Men are allowing just 184.9 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. However, New York has yielded 14 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

free_agents.name: Jared Goff
free_agents.outlook: Jared Goff will aim to return to dominance as the Lions travel to Miami in Week 9. Goff finished Week 8 against a tough Minnesota defense with his worst fantasy performance of the season, completing 18 of 25 passes for 176 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. The veteran quarterback still has excellent figures this year with 1,964 passing yards 15 touchdowns and one pick across seven games. He'll face a Dolphins defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign.

free_agents.name: Jordan Love
free_agents.outlook: Jordan Love will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Love stayed hot in a Week 8 win over the Panthers, completing 30 of 41 passes for 288 yards with a 3:1 TD:INT ratio. He's now thrown for 250-plus yards in six of eight games and recorded two or more touchdowns in every outing of the season. Love will face a New England defense that ceded 211 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to his former backup, Malik Willis, this past weekend.

free_agents.name: Rachaad White
free_agents.outlook: Rachaad White has scored in back-to-back games for Washington. White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. White has found the end zone in each of the last two contests since taking over the starting running back job for the injured Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Jeremy McNichols also left this game with an injury, leaving Austin Ekeler as the only other healthy option. In Week 9, Washington will face a Rams defense allowing 109.3 yards per tilt on the ground, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Rams have surrendered just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for third in the league.

free_agents.name: Dalton Kincaid
free_agents.outlook: Dalton Kincaid faces a challenging matchup in Week 9 when the Bills face the Vikings. He has 11 catches over the last two weeks, scoring in Week 8 for the first time since Week 2, and finished with 86 yards after hauling in just 90 total yards in his previous four games. Minnesota has allowed the fewest points per game to opposing tight ends, surrendering only 6.2 yards per target and no touchdowns through seven games. Kincaid needs volume to be productive in the Week 9 Monday night affair, and that's not a sure thing.

free_agents.name: Hunter Henry
free_agents.outlook: Hunter Henry will need to overcome a foot injury if he's to help the Patriots loosen up a stingy Packers defense in Week 9. Henry hauled in all three of his first-half targets in Week 8 before exiting. Should he play, the challenge becomes finding holes against a Green Bay defense that's allowing just 5.8 yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends. Eli Raridon has shown promise and would benefit from a potential Henry absence, but the matchup concerns remain.

free_agents.name: Jakobi Meyers
free_agents.outlook: Jakobi Meyers was held to two catches in Week 8 while playing through a hamstring injury. He has had an up-and-down season for the Jaguars while working as the No. 2 WR behind Parker Washington. The Jaguars visit the Ravens on Thursday in Week 9, so Meyers may not have time to regain health on a short week. The injury risk lowers his floor, but he's a passable flex option against a Ravens defense that's giving up 177.6 yards per game to wideouts. Meyers is averaging 3.1 catches for 44.1 yards per game, with two TDs in seven outings.

free_agents.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Marvin Harrison has drawn four targets in each of his first two games with the Texans. The 2024 fourth overall pick of the Cardinals could start to earn a larger role with his new team, especially after having a chance to further familiarize himself with the playbook during Houston's Week 8 bye. Harrison won't be a recommended fantasy option until he earns a larger role, as he played just 19% of offensive snaps in his Texans debut and 21% in his second game with the team. He'll be a risky Week 9 option against the Chargers' mediocre secondary, but Harrison's future looks brighter in Houston than it did in Arizona.

free_agents.name: Cam Little
free_agents.outlook: Cam Little has attempted 23 PATs compared to just 12 field goals this season, a testament to Jacksonville's high-octane offense. His ceiling remains immense given the frequent scoring opportunities and Little's elite range, making him a viable fantasy starter for Week 9. Little will face a reeling Ravens team in Week 9 that has dropped three consecutive games while allowing at least 35 points in each of the last two. Overall, Baltimore has given up 16 made field goals in eight games while allowing 25.4 points per game.

free_agents.name: Tyler Bass
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Bass has been busy for the Bills ahead of a difficult Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. He has multiple field goals in four straight weeks, 12 in total. Bass has added upside to his stable floor in Buffalo's high-scoring offense, which has yielded 21 extra points in seven games. Minnesota has allowed only six field goals and 11 made PATs all season, putting Bass' hot streak in jeopardy.

free_agents.name: Kirk Cousins
free_agents.outlook: Kirk Cousins is coming off arguably his best performance of 2026, completing a season-high 73.1% of his passes and tossing three touchdowns in a Week 8 win over the Jets. He also ran for his first score of the year. Cousins' 19 TD passes through eight games puts him second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow's 20, and his 2,124 passing yards puts him third behind Matthew Stafford (2,146) and Jordan Love (2,246). As long as Cousins keeps producing at a high level and the Raiders are in the playoff picture, rookie Fernando Mendoza should remain on the bench. Cousins faces a tougher test in Week 9 against a 49ers defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Kyler Murray
free_agents.outlook: Kyler Murray will look to get healed ahead of Minnesota's Week 9 matchup against Buffalo. Murray completed 17 of 29 passes for 210 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, along with four rushes for 35 yards in a Week 8 loss to Detroit. The veteran was also dealing with hamstring tightness throughout the game, but a full week of practice should mitigate the injury. Barring any major setbacks, Murray will face a Bills defense that's ranked a favorable 28th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

free_agents.name: Matt Gay
free_agents.outlook: Matt Gay was perfect in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets, converting all five of his PATs and his only field goal attempt. The veteran kicker has missed just two FGs through eight games this season, going 18-for-20 (90.0%), and he's drilled all 19 of his extra points. Playing his home games indoors appears to suit Gay, after he connected on just 13 of 19 field goals during his 10-game stint with the Commanders in 2025. Gay likely can't afford to squander any opportunities in Week 9 against a 49ers team allowing just 19.9 points per game, tied for sixth in the league.

free_agents.name: Tyler Loop
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Loop and the Ravens are back home for a Week 9 clash against the 5-2 Jaguars. He went 1-for-2 on field goal attempts and converted his lone PAT during Baltimore's 36-10 loss in Week 8. Loop has attempted more than two FGs just once this season, and there's a good chance his limited involvement will continue with Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) probably done for the year. The Ravens have scored a combined 33 points over their last three outings, and their struggles are likely to persist versus a Jacksonville defense allowing just 15.9 points per game, the second-best mark in the league.

free_agents.name: Bo Nix
free_agents.outlook: Bo Nix put together another fourth-quarter comeback in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City. While the third-year QB's own numbers are nothing special this season, he's led his team to a 6-2 record and first place in the AFC West. Week 8 was only the second time in eight games he's thrown for multiple touchdowns, and his 59.6% completion rate and 6.0 yards per attempt are both career lows. Nix could be poised for his best game of the season in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and is tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Jonah Coleman
free_agents.outlook: Jonah Coleman may be emerging as the Broncos' lead running back. The 2026 fourth-round pick topped 100 scrimmage yards for the first time in a comeback win over Kansas City in Week 8, and he scored the winning touchdown on a five-yard run after getting Denver into the red zone with a 51-yard catch-and-run. J.K. Dobbins logged seven carries, compared to Coleman's 15 total touches, and with RJ Harvey on injured reserve, the path is clear for the rookie to handle a significant workload. Coleman could be headed for a true breakout performance in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that just fired its defensive coordinator and ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: DeMario Douglas
free_agents.outlook: DeMario Douglas' volume has been sporadic despite the Patriots' receiving corps rarely being at full strength entering a Week 9 matchup with the Packers. Douglas has four touchdowns over his last four games, but he has four or fewer targets in half of New England's eight games, failing to top 23 yards at the same rate. Green Bay is allowing just 7.0 yards per target to wideouts, suggesting Douglas would need to maintain his scoring prowess to be a viable Week 9 option.

free_agents.name: Kenny Gainwell
free_agents.outlook: Kenny Gainwell will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He racked up a career-high 140 rushing yards on 25 carries in the Week 8 win over the Falcons, bringing his season total to 289 yards (5.0 yards per carry). Despite Gainwell's huge performance, he still remains firmly behind Bucky Irving in the Buccaneers' backfield. Gainwell could struggle, especially against a strong Bears defense that has allowed just three rushing touchdowns to RBs all season.

free_agents.name: Brenton Strange
free_agents.outlook: Brenton Strange leads the Jaguars with 28 catches this season and has averaged 65.5 receiving yards over the past four games after averaging a meager 24 yards per game through Week 3. Despite the recent uptick in production, he hasn't scored a TD since Week 1. Strange has a nice opportunity to end his touchdown drought in Week 9 against the Ravens, who have allowed six TDs to TEs, which is tied for fourth-most in the NFL. Given Strange's recent involvement and the favorable matchup, he's worth starting in Week 9.

free_agents.name: Jake Ferguson
free_agents.outlook: Jake Ferguson left the last game for Dallas due to an ankle injury. His status remains up in the air for Week 9 versus Indianapolis. Ferguson has failed to register a single catch in each of the last two contests. Brevyn Spann-Ford could see additional looks if Ferguson is sidelined. Spann-Ford snagged five passes for 31 yards following Ferguson's departure. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Brian Thomas has caught just one of seven targets over Jacksonville's past three games, but at least that one catch went for a 12-yard touchdown in Week 8 against the Colts. Jacksonville is reportedly open to trading the 2024 first-round pick, so perhaps Thomas will be more involved in the Week 9 game plan against the Ravens to showcase his skills. The Jaguars may be able to pull away from a Ravens team that's starting its third-string QB and feed Thomas targets against a Baltimore defense that's allowing 177.6 yards per game to WRs. Thomas could be worth a speculative add if he was dropped in your league since a change of scenery could boost his value, but the upside of a possible uptick in Week 9 usage is overshadowed by the fact he has just one catch in the last three games, so Thomas is best left on the bench.

free_agents.name: MarShawn Lloyd
free_agents.outlook: MarShawn Lloyd will look to make the most of his touches as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Lloyd logged his lowest touch total of the year in a Week 8 win over Carolina, rushing the ball three times for seven yards and catching one pass for nine yards. While starting running back Josh Jacobs' status remains uncertain in the coming weeks, Lloyd's production even when Jacobs was inactive makes him a risky option. New England has ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

free_agents.name: Geno Smith
free_agents.outlook: Geno Smith faces an uphill battle to continue his current form when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. Smith has thrown for multiple touchdowns and at least 287 yards in consecutive weeks after tossing only one or no touchdowns in five of his first six outings. Kansas City has allowed only seven touchdown passes, with only two opposing quarterbacks topping 222 yards against them, suggesting fantasy managers are better off looking for streaming options elsewhere.

free_agents.name: Sam Darnold
free_agents.outlook: Sam Darnold has struggled to avoid turnovers this season heading into Seattle's Week 9 matchup versus Arizona. Darnold tossed a pickoff against Chicago in Week 8, giving him at least one interception in each of the six games he's completed so far in 2026. Darnold did throw two touchdowns in the loss, but he also completed just half of his 34 pass attempts. He has an opportunity to get right against the Cardinals, who are allowing a 110.4 QB rating on the season, second-worst in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Robinson has been sidelined for two consecutive games due to a hamstring issue. However, he's been an effective runner when healthy, averaging 4.0 yards per carry and rushing for four touchdowns in six appearances this season. Despite this, he'll likely need to find the end zone to be fantasy relevant against a Bengals defense that's given up just 19.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this year.

free_agents.name: Keon Coleman
free_agents.outlook: Keon Coleman will benefit if DJ Moore is sidelined ahead of the Bills' Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. Coleman was held to just one catch in Week 8, the fourth time that's occurred in seven games, with three of those coinciding with Moore on the field. Moore is again dealing with a knee issue that's believed to be minor, but even if he's unable to play in Week 9, Coleman's potential against a defense that's allowed only four touchdown passes in seven games likely isn't appealing.

free_agents.name: Chad Ryland
free_agents.outlook: Chad Ryland is coming off a roller-coaster performance as Arizona prepares to visit Seattle in Week 9. Ryland missed an extra-point attempt in Week 8 versus Dallas that would have given Arizona a one-point lead with about one minute left in the game, but he rebounded by making a game-winning 42-yard field goal in overtime. The PAT miss was his first of the season, and he's gone 19-of-21 on FG attempts, so Ryland is secure in his role as the Cardinals' kicker. His opportunities may be limited against a Seattle defense that is giving up the eighth-fewest points in the league.

free_agents.name: Cairo Santos
free_agents.outlook: Cairo Santos will look to build on a solid showing as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Santos made all of his kicks in Chicago's Week 8 win over the Seahawks, nailing two field goal attempts and four XPAs. The veteran kicker had also missed a field goal in three straight games before this matchup, so he's hopefully now back on track. Tampa Bay has ranked 13th in fantasy points allowed to kickers so far this campaign.

free_agents.name: Tank Dell
free_agents.outlook: Tank Dell made his season debut in Week 7, ahead of Houston's Week 8 bye. The 2023 third-round pick showcased his trademark big-play ability with a 43-yard catch on his only target. This was Dell's first game action since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign due to a knee injury. The Texans also have Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte vying for snaps at wide receiver, which makes Dell a risky Week 9 fantasy option against the Chargers. The Chargers rank in the middle of the pack at defending WRs. Dell is worth stashing on the bench, as he delivered starter-level fantasy production prior to his extended absence, but he'll need to increase his involvement to regain fantasy relevance.

free_agents.name: Baker Mayfield
free_agents.outlook: Baker Mayfield is expected to lead the Buccaneers' passing game into the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He was the first quarterback since 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass, doing so in a rainy Week 8 divisional matchup against the Falcons. Since returning from injury in Week 7, Mayfield has attempted just 14 total passes, partially due to last week's rainy conditions. However, offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has heavily leaned on the ground game over the last four weeks, which is a poor sign for Mayfield's fantasy outlook. Mayfield is still in for a favorable Week 9 matchup against a Bears defense that has allowed 22.3 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through seven contests.

free_agents.name: Kendre Miller
free_agents.outlook: Kendre Miller is expected to operate as the Saints' top rusher in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. While Travis Etienne (hamstring) has been sidelined, Miller has averaged 11 carries per game, but just 28.8 rushing yards per game (2.6 yards per carry). Despite the lack of efficiency, Miller has led New Orleans' backfield in carries three consecutive games, which bodes well for his outlook while Etienne remains out. Miller could find success against the Browns' defense in Week 9, as they've given up 4.9 yards per carry to opposing running backs this season.

free_agents.name: Quentin Johnston
free_agents.outlook: Quentin Johnston remains mostly an afterthought in the Chargers' struggling passing game. The fourth-year wide receiver caught a season-high four passes in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, but turned them into just 37 receiving yards. Johnston hasn't seen more than six targets in any of his six appearances this year, piecing together a 12-202-0 line on 26 targets. He might be able to make an impact on limited volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans secondary that ranks a stunning 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Rashid Shaheed
free_agents.outlook: Rashid Shaheed will look to return from a knee injury in time to suit up for Seattle's Week 9 battle against Arizona. Shaheed missed the Week 8 loss to Chicago due to the injury, and it's unclear how close he is to returning to action. Should he be able to return to face the Cardinals, he'll have a good opportunity for success against a suspect Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals have given up 25 receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the league.

free_agents.name: Dalton Schultz
free_agents.outlook: Dalton Schultz isn't a recommended Week 9 fantasy option in most formats for Houston's road game against the Chargers. The veteran TE has 33 catches for 322 yards through Houston's first seven games of the season, but Schultz has yet to score this season, and the Chargers have allowed just one TD to a TE. Frustratingly for Schultz's fantasy managers, backup TE Foster Moreau has scored three TDs on 11 catches this season.

free_agents.name: Kaelon Black
free_agents.outlook: Kaelon Black may have an opportunity for more work in Week 9 versus the Raiders with San Francisco's top RB, Christian McCaffrey, managing a hamstring strain. McCaffrey picked up the injury in Week 7 against Atlanta, and Black ended up logging a healthy 12 carries, which he turned into 63 yards and a touchdown. McCaffrey was able to finish out that game, and the team's Week 8 bye along with optimism that the strain is mild gives him a good chance of suiting up this Sunday, but Black could be productive even if McCaffrey plays. Las Vegas has posted some of the worst numbers in the NFL against running backs, giving up 22.3 fantasy points per game to the position, fifth-most in the league.

free_agents.name: Evan McPherson
free_agents.outlook: Evan McPherson and the Bengals travel to take on the Falcons for a Week 9 interconference tilt in Spain. He made all five of his PATs for the second consecutive game during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime victory in Week 8. It was also the second time in as many weeks that McPherson did not attempt a field goal, as Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense racked up six total TDs in the win. McPherson has yet to miss a single kick in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 24-for-24 on PATs, but his fantasy ceiling is seemingly capped with Cincinnati frequently finding the endzone.

free_agents.name: Seth McGowan
free_agents.outlook: Seth McGowan is averaging fewer than five carries per game while posting just four catches in his first eight NFL games. The rookie seventh-round pick won't be a recommended fantasy option for Week 9 against the Cowboys if it's business as usual in the Colts' backfield, but trade rumors have been brewing around star RB Jonathan Taylor. If Taylor is traded or held out in anticipation of a trade, McGowan or DJ Giddens would be the next man up. Should McGowan garner a starter's workload, he would be a serviceable fantasy RB2 in Week 9 against a dreadful Dallas defense that's allowing 144.5 scrimmage yards per game to RBs and has given up 11 TDs to the position in eight games.

free_agents.name: Dontayvion Wicks
free_agents.outlook: Dontayvion Wicks missed yet another game for the Eagles due to a balky ankle. In fact, Wicks has missed the last two contests because of the ailment.  If he is somehow able to suit up in Week 9, he would be facing a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 184.9 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jayden Reed
free_agents.outlook: Jayden Reed will remain out as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams, Bo Melton and  J. Michael Sturdivant to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

free_agents.name: Michael Penix Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Michael Penix will look to rebound from a poor Week 8 performance in the Falcons' Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Penix really struggled in last week's loss to the Buccaneers, completing just eight of 24 passes for 125 yards and four interceptions while playing in heavy rain. He could very well bounce back in Week 9, however, as Cincinnati's defense has allowed 22.1 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Additionally, the Bengals' defense just allowed Cam Ward to throw for 304  yards and two touchdowns in a Week 8 win, which bodes well for Penix's outlook this coming week.

free_agents.name: Mike Washington Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Mike Washington may be in the process of taking over the early-down role in the Raiders' backfield. The rookie saw a career-high 25 carries in a Week 8 win over the Jets, turning them into 83 yards, while Ashton Jeanty mainly saw usage as a pass catcher and got only two carries. Washington's been far more effective on the ground, averaging 4.3 yards per carry to Jeanty's 3.1 mark, so the move from coach Klint Kubiak seems long overdue. The workload split could tip back toward Jeanty depending on the matchup, and a Week 9 tilt against the 49ers likely favors him over Washington. San Francisco's defense ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but 32nd in the league in receptions allowed to the position.

free_agents.name: J.J. McCarthy
free_agents.outlook: J.J. McCarthy comes off the bye as the starting quarterback of the first-place Giants as they head into a divisional matchup in Week 9 versus bumbling Philadelphia. The Eagles have lost six-straight contests. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL. Meanwhile, McCarthy has thrown for at least 243 yards in each of the last two games for the G-Men.

free_agents.name: Kimani Vidal
free_agents.outlook: Kimani Vidal remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Omarion Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Keaton Mitchell got seven touches and Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Vidal does have two TDs in the last four games, one rushing and one receiving, but his current usage gives him little upside. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Mike Gesicki
free_agents.outlook: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Spain for a Week 9 interconference tilt against the Falcons. He caught four of six targets for 76 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in Week 8. The 76 receiving yards were Gesicki's most in a game since he went for 78 in the season opener, and the 31-year-old was able to extend his streak of outings with a TD catch to five. He now owns a 17-241-6 line on 24 targets through seven contests and will try to make it six straight with a score versus an Atlanta defense allowing 14.4 fantasy points per game (T-20th) to TEs.

free_agents.name: Isiah Pacheco
free_agents.outlook: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 9 as the Lions travel to Miami. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

free_agents.name: Chig Okonkwo
free_agents.outlook: Chig Okonkwo made a dazzling one-handed catch last game for Washington. The highlight-reel grab is a candidate for one of the top receptions of the NFL season to date. Okonkwo finished with two catches for 32 yards in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. He was targeted four times. In Week 9, Okonkwo will face a stellar Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.

free_agents.name: Samaje Perine
free_agents.outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to Spain for a Week 9 clash against the Falcons. He rushed four times for 10 yards and caught his only target for nine yards during Cincinnati's overtime victory in Week 8. Perine played 33% of the offensive snaps but was unable to produce much on a day the Bengals put up a season-high 43 points. He'll aim to get more involved against an Atlanta defense that ranks 30th, giving up 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.

free_agents.name: Tyler Higbee
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Higbee will look to snap a recent downturn in production when the Rams take on the Commanders in Week 9. After logging at least five catches and at least 62 yards in three straight games Weeks 3-5, Higbee has topped out at four receptions and 22 yards over his past three contests. The problem hasn't been opportunity -- in fact, Higbee's offensive snap share has actually increased during the more recent three-game span. He could rediscover success against a Washington defense that has given up the second-most fantasy points per game (14.4) to tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Deshaun Watson
free_agents.outlook: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit New Orleans for an interconference clash in Week 9. He completed 27 of 39 pass attempts for 324 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed three times for two yards during Cleveland's 27-6 loss in Week 8. Watson lost a fumble and was sacked eight times in another tough showing for the Browns' offense. He'll try to turn things around against a Saints defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-14th) to opposing QBs.

free_agents.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Rodriguez is the clear No. 2 RB for the Jaguars behind Bhayshul Tuten heading into a Week 9 trip to Baltimore. Rodriguez has made the most of his opportunities, setting season highs in scrimmage yards in each of the past two games, with 55 in Week 6 against the Texans and 58 in Week 8 against the Colts. He remains a touchdown-dependent fantasy option for Week 9, as Rodriguez has just two catches this season and is averaging just under seven touches per game overall. The Ravens have allowed seven rushing scores to RBs in eight games, but there's an elevated chance of the Jaguars pulling away and leaning on Rodriguez more to run out the clock since Baltimore could be down to its third-string QB.

free_agents.name: Mason Taylor
free_agents.outlook: Mason Taylor brings potential in a favorable matchup for the Jets against the Chiefs in Week 9. Taylor earned five targets in Week 8, his third straight game with at least that many looks, but he converted them into just 19 yards on three catches. That matchup came against the Raiders, who allow the fourth-most fantasy points to tight ends. The Chiefs allow the fifth most, with five of the seven touchdown receptions they've surrendered coming from the position. Though Taylor failed to capitalize in a plus spot, the opportunity is there again.

free_agents.name: Daniel Jones
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Jones has consistently finished outside the top 20 fantasy QBs this season, and that's unlikely to change in Week 9, even in a favorable home matchup against the Cowboys. The 2-6 Colts have gone into sell mode while dropping four consecutive games, and Jones has a 2:5 TD:INT ratio during the four-game losing streak. He has fallen short of 150 passing yards in each of his last two starts, as Jones' season average has dropped below 200 passing yards per game. Dallas has given up a 15:3 TD:INT ratio and fell apart against Gardner Minshew and the Cardinals, but Jones has yet to post a multi-TD performance, so the plus matchup puts him in the starting conversation for superflex formats but not single-QB leagues.

free_agents.name: Adonai Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Adonai Mitchell faces an uphill battle if he hopes to repeat a career outing when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. After being shut out since Week 2, Mitchell popped for seven catches, 142 yards, and a touchdown in Week 8, shifting the spotlight from surging rookie Omar Cooper. Mitchell has always shown big-play potential but sees inconsistent opportunities. This sets him up as a high-potential, low-ceiling option against a Chiefs secondary that's allowing just 6.9 yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wideouts.

free_agents.name: Keaton Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Keaton Mitchell remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Omarion Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Mitchell got seven touches and Kimani Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Mitchell is still looking for his first rushing TD of the season, and his current usage holds little appeal. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Darius Cooper
free_agents.outlook: Darius Cooper finished second on the Eagles in targets last game behind Makai Lemon. With starting wideouts DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks both sidelined due to injury, Cooper saw an increase in looks. Unfortunately, Cooper could only manage two catches for 19 yards in the dismal 27-10 loss to the Commanders. Cooper has just 11 catches on the season. In Week 9, the Eagles will face a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 189.4 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Malik Willis
free_agents.outlook: Malik Willis will look to extend his multi-touchdown pass streak to three games in an inviting Week 9 matchup for the Dolphins against the Lions. Willis isn't taking many downfield chances, limiting him to a season-high of 220 passing yards, but he has four touchdowns over the last two weeks after just two in his first five games prior to Miami's Week 6 bye. Detroit has been the league's worst defense against quarterbacks, surrendering 18 touchdown passes through seven games, and while Willis hasn't run as often as expected, he'll carry some intrigue as a potential Week 9 streaming option in deeper formats.

free_agents.name: Rashod Bateman
free_agents.outlook: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens return home to face the Jaguars in Week 9. He caught one of three targets for 22 yards during Baltimore's 36-10 loss in Week 8. Bateman led the team in yardage after both Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) and Tyler Huntley (toe) were forced out of the contest with injuries, which should tell you all you need to know about the current state of the Ravens' offense. Bateman should be left on fantasy benches/waiver wires despite facing the Jaguars' 29th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs.

free_agents.name: Roschon Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Roschon Johnson could return to being a depth option as the Bears play Tampa Bay in Week 9. Johnson has benefited from the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) during the last four weeks, as he's averaging 9.5 touches per game in this stretch. Unfortunately, Monangai could return in the upcoming home front, which would shrink Johnson's role. Even if Monangai sits out again, Johnson would be a tough play against a Bucs defense that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.

free_agents.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Fitzgerald likely won't have many scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Fitzgerald was perfect in the Week 8 loss to the Packers, making all three of his kicks (two field goals and one extra point). On the season, Fitzgerald has converted on all 13 of his field goal tries but just 13 of his 18 point-after attempts. He could have few scoring chances against the Broncos as well, with Denver's defense allowing just 7.6 kicking points per game this year.

free_agents.name: Kalif Raymond
free_agents.outlook: Kalif Raymond remains a secondary option in Chicago's offense heading into Week 9 against Tampa Bay. Raymond finished a Week 8 win over the Seahawks with two catches for 14 yards, and he tacked on one rush for 39 yards. The veteran has taken a major backseat to Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the WR hierarchy at this point in the season, but he's still a reliable option when needed for quarterback Caleb Williams. Raymond will face a Bucs defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Darren Waller
free_agents.outlook: Darren Waller will look to bounce back from another poor performance in Carolina's Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Waller has underwhelmed over the last two weeks, catching just two of four targets for 61 yards and a touchdown. Despite this, he still ranks first amongst Panthers tight ends in targets (24), yards (209) and touchdown (three), though he still likely isn't reliable enough to be a weekly starter. Waller could have success against Denver in Week 9, however, as its defense has allowed 16.9 fantasy points per game to tight ends this season, the sixth-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Cooper Kupp
free_agents.outlook: Cooper Kupp heads into Seattle's Week 9 matchup versus the Cardinals looking for a more impactful role in his team's offense. Kupp caught a touchdown in Week 8 against the Bears, but the seven-yard score was his only reception of the game. With three of fewer targets in six of his eight contests on the campaign, Kupp simply isn't getting much of an opportunity to be productive when he isn't getting into the end zone. The Cardinals do present a good matchup, as they've yielded 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for the most in the league.

free_agents.name: Jerry Jeudy
free_agents.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns visit the Saints for an interconference clash in Week 9. He was unable to catch his lone target during Cleveland's 27-6 loss in Week 8, marking his third outing of the season without a catch. Jeudy had four receptions in each of his last two contests prior to getting blanked, and he now boasts a 16-171-0 line on 24 targets over eight games. He'll try to rebound versus a New Orleans defense that ranks 15th in terms of fantasy points allowed per game (30.2) to opposing WRs.

free_agents.name: Corey Kiner
free_agents.outlook: Corey Kiner has had a minimal role in the Patriots' backfield entering a Week 9 matchup with the Packers. Kiner has rushed for 38 yards or more in three of the last four games, despite Rhamondre Stevenson leading the way in touches and TreVeyon Henderson factoring in when healthy. If Henderson were sidelined again in Week 9, Kiner may still not gather enough volume to be an option against a defense that's allowing 3.96 yards per carry.

free_agents.name: Bam Knight
free_agents.outlook: Bam Knight's status for Arizona's Week 9 battle in Seattle is in question due to a concussion he suffered this past Sunday. The head injury happened when Knight took a shoulder from a Dallas defender to his helmet, and he subsequently entered concussion protocol. He'll need to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before being eligible for game action again, but if he is able to play in Week 9, he could see a decent share of action given that No. 1 RB Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury. The Arizona run game could struggle against a Seattle defense that is giving up just 3.28 yards per carry to running backs, though Chicago's D'Andre Swift did just burn the Seahawks for three rushing scores on Monday Night Football.

free_agents.name: Jaylin Noel
free_agents.outlook: Jaylin Noel sustained a season-ending toe injury in Houston's Week 7 loss to the Giants. The 2025 third-round pick can be dropped in all redraft formats ahead of Houston's Week 9 road game against the Chargers. Noel was gaining momentum prior to getting hurt, so he has some forward-looking value in dynasty and keeper formats.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens return home for a meeting with the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. He rushed three times for 15 yards and caught four of eight targets for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 8 loss. Hill led the team in receptions and targets while finishing second in yardage in a game where the Ravens managed just 167 total yards of offense. He could earn similar opportunities with Lamar Jackson (thumb) on IR and Joe Fagnano (knee) likely to start, but it's going to be difficult to trust any Baltimore player in fantasy going forward.

free_agents.name: Tez Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Tez Johnson is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top pass-catchers in the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. His offensive role expanded with Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) sidelined over the last two weeks. However, Johnson has logged just two receptions for 33 yards and a touchdown during that span, largely because Tampa Bay attempted just 14 total passes. While the Buccaneers' offense remains extremely run-heavy, Johnson will likely be irrelevant for fantasy purposes without finding the end zone. He could struggle against a Bears secondary that's allowed just seven total touchdowns to wideouts this season.

free_agents.name: AJ Barner
free_agents.outlook: AJ Barner continues to put together a quiet campaign for Seattle heading into a Week 9 matchup against the Cardinals. Though Barner has consistently logged high offensive snap shares as the Seahawks' No. 1 tight end, he's exceeded three catches just twice through eight contests. Against Chicago in Week 8, he put up a modest 2-23-0 line but did draw five targets, tying his second-highest mark this season. Barner may be able to be more efficient against the Cardinals, who have allowed a 78.6% catch rate to tight ends, tied for fourth-highest in the league.

free_agents.name: Treylon Burks
free_agents.outlook: Treylon Burks led the Commanders in receiving last game. Burks caught three passes for 81 yards in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. Burks has at least five targets in three-straight tilts. However, in Week 9, Burks will face a superb Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.

free_agents.name: Jake Elliott
free_agents.outlook: Jake Elliott has made just two field goals over his last four games for the Eagles. The Philadelphia offense has sputtered due to a bevy of injuries, scoring fewer than 20 points in three of those four contests. That has led to limited opportunities for Elliott, who also missed a three-pointer in the most recent loss to Washington. In Week 9, the Eagles will face division-leading New York. The Giants are allowing 23 points per tilt, which is 15th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Nick Folk
free_agents.outlook: Nick Folk could have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Folk struggled in the pouring rain during the Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, missing his only field goal try of the game. On the season, the veteran kicker has converted just 12 of 16 field goal attempts and 15 of 16 point-after tries. He could find success in Week 9, however, as Cincinnati's defense has allowed 8.0 kicking points per game this season.

free_agents.name: Wil Lutz
free_agents.outlook: Wil Lutz hasn't missed a kick in three straight games, connecting on both his field goal attempts and both his PATs in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City. The veteran kicker is a perfect 14-for-14 on extra points this season, but his 82.4% showing on FG attempts (14-for-17, including two misses from inside 50 yards) would be his worst mark in four years since following Sean Payton to Denver from New Orleans. Lutz could see plenty of opportunities to improve that performance in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator after allowing 27.6 points a game, 28th in the league, through the first half of the season.

free_agents.name: Malachi Fields
free_agents.outlook: Malachi Fields is coming off a career-best performance for the Giants. Fields snagged four passes for 83 yards in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. The rookie has caught at least two passes in every game in 2026. In Week 9, the Giants face divisional rival Philadelphia, which has struggled to defend the pass. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Pierre Strong Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Pierre Strong is primed to be a depth option again as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. The continued presence of Josh Jacobs has knocked Strong down a peg, and he's logged just one carry for two yards in the last two weeks. With Chris Brooks now vying for a return off IR and MarShawn Lloyd remaining the complementary option to Jacobs, Strong's role could diminish fully in the coming weeks. New England's front has ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Devin Singletary
free_agents.outlook: Singletary scored the winning touchdown last game for the Giants, and could have a larger role in the backfield moving forward. Tyrone Tracy was placed on Injured Reserve following the most recent contest, leaving only Singletary and Cam Skattebo as the healthy options out of the backfield. Though talks of a trade for Jonathan Taylor have intensified, nothing appears imminent heading into a tasty Week 9 clash with Philadelphia. The Eagles have been torched on the ground in 2026, allowing 131.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. Likewise, the Eagles have given up 10 rushing scores, which is tied for 24th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jaydon Blue
free_agents.outlook: Jaydon Blue was initially thought to be the backup to Saquon Barkley last game, but it was Elijah Mitchell who led the Eagles in rushing. In fact, Blue did not even register a carry in the 27-10 loss to the Commanders. Barkley has been assured he will not be traded, leaving Blue as an afterthought, and perhaps even behind Mitchell on the depth chart. However, a potentially juicy matchup is on the horizon in Week 9 versus the Giants, especially if Barkley is not on the field. New York is allowing 128.1 rushing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jason Sanders
free_agents.outlook: Jason Sanders' opportunities have been uneven for the Jets ahead of a Week 9 game against the Chiefs. For the second time in three weeks and third time overall in Week 8, Sanders attempted four field goals. Unfortunately, he has four games with just one made 3-pointer, while three times collecting one or zero PATs. Kansas City has allowed 15 field goals through seven games but only 10 PATs, so while suggesting the Jets will have stalled drives is fair, field goals likely won't keep them competitive, making Sanders a risky Week 9 option.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor finally began to show some chemistry with Kirk Cousins in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets. Nailor set new season highs in receptions (four) and receiving yards (38) while hauling in his first touchdown of the year. The former Viking should continue seeing a big workload in terms of snaps due to his blocking ability and unselfish route running, but Nailor seems firmly behind Brock Bowers, Tre Tucker and Ashton Jeanty in the pecking order for targets. Nailor isn't likely to make a big impact in Week 9 against a 49ers secondary that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Elijah Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Elijah Mitchell led the Eagles in rushing last game. Jaydon Blue was initially thought to be the primary backup to Saquon Barkley, but it was Mitchell who led the Eagles with 34 yards on the ground. In fact, Blue did not even register a carry in the 27-10 loss to the Commanders. Barkley has been assured he will not be traded, leaving Blue as an afterthought, and perhaps even behind Mitchell on the depth chart. Meanwhile, a potentially juicy matchup is on the horizon in Week 9 versus the Giants for whomever is the bell cow. New York is allowing 128.1 rushing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jaylen Wright
free_agents.outlook: Jaylen Wright continues to play a minor role in the Dolphins' rushing game ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Lions. Wright has logged a 12% to 14% snap share over the last three weeks, not topping six offensive touches in any outing, with Ollie Gordon dominating carries. Detroit is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, which is in the middle of the pack, but they allow the third-fewest fantasy points to the position. Barring an injury to Gordon, Wright's usage is unlikely to change, keeping him off most fantasy radars.

free_agents.name: Konata Mumpfield
free_agents.outlook: Konata Mumpfield is still looking to break out ahead of the Rams' Week 9 clash against the Commanders. Mumpfield has logged at least 26 offensive snaps each of the past three weeks, but he's managed just three catches for 30 yards on seven targets during that span. There's opportunity for him to increase his production with Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR for multiple more weeks, but to this point Mumpfield hasn't been able to form chemistry with QB Matthew Stafford. He may need to get into the end zone to be fantasy-relevant, and Washington is tied for 18th in the league by giving up seven touchdowns to wideouts through seven games.

free_agents.name: Cade Otton
free_agents.outlook: Cade Otton is expected to serve as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has caught just one pass over Tampa Bay's last three games, making him hard to trust going forward. Since Baker Mayfield returned from injury in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, the Buccaneers have attempted just 14 passes, making it hard for their pass catchers to contribute to fantasy teams. Despite this, Otton is in for a relatively favorable Week 9 matchup against a Chicago defense that's allowed 13.1 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends through seven contests this season.

free_agents.name: Jahan Dotson
free_agents.outlook: Jahan Dotson is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top wideouts in the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Dotson was one of the few bright spots in Atlanta's Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, catching two of five targets for a game-high 95 yards. Dotson has been finding his groove as the Falcons' No. 2 WR as of late, recording more than 50 receiving yards in four of his last five games. He could find success against a Bengals secondary that's given up eight receiving touchdowns to WRs in just seven contests this season.

free_agents.name: Efton Chism III
free_agents.outlook: Efton Chism hasn't provided chunk plays in the Patriots offense ahead of a Week 9 matchup with Green Bay. Chism drew five targets in Week 8 with A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined, an uptick from the two targets he collected over the previous two games with Brown on the field. His season-high has been 57 yards, not offering much potential. Even if Brown remains sidelined, Chism isn't likely to be a preferred option for Drake Maye or fantasy lineups against a secondary that's allowing 7.0 yards per target.

free_agents.name: Tyler Huntley
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Huntley and the Ravens host the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. He moved to the backup role with Lamar Jackson finally making his return from an ankle injury in Week 8, but Huntley was forced back into action after Jackson injured the thumb on his throwing hand on Baltimore's first offensive snap. Huntley appears to have picked up a toe injury of his own, as third stringer Joe Fagnano replaced him in the third quarter of the Ravens' 36-10 loss. Huntley should be considered questionable to play versus Jacksonville, but even if he's able to suit up, he belongs on fantasy benches in a difficult matchup on a short week.

free_agents.name: Chris Brooks
free_agents.outlook: Chris Brooks will aim to make a return as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Brooks has been on IR for the last four weeks due to an ankle injury, but he could be on the field as soon as this week if his recovery allows it. The fourth-year running back remained a solid change-of-pace option in the first four weeks of the season, with excellent pass blocking that kept him involved. If he does play against New England, he's set to be an option in a backfield consisting of Josh Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd and minimally Pierre Strong.

free_agents.name: Jauan Jennings
free_agents.outlook: Jauan Jennings will look to stay involved as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jennings brought in two catches for 11 yards in Minnesota's Week 8 loss to the Lions, which was his second straight game with two catches. The veteran pass catcher has now logged six receptions for 54 yards on 10 targets this season. He could see continued success against a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to his position.
